answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via time-locked stake bonding. Each agent deposits collateral into an escrow contract with a strict unbonding delay, blocking flash-loan cycling and anchoring a harbor against a sudden tide of fake identities. Attackers incur the verifiable opportunity cost of locked capital and slashing penalties for equivocation per identity, forming a costly reef against spam. However, capital gates bar unfunded builders and weaken if token value collapses.
